description_full: American Coastal Insurance Corporation, through its subsidiaries, primarily engages in the commercial and personal property and casualty insurance business in the United States. The company provides structure, content, and liability coverage for standard single-family homeowners, renters, and condominium unit owners. It also offers commercial multi-peril property insurance for residential condominium associations and apartments, as well as coverage to policyholders for loss or damage to buildings, inventory, and equipment caused by fire, wind, hail, water, theft, and vandalism. In addition, the company provides equipment breakdown, identity theft, and flood policies. The company markets and distributes its products through a network of independent agencies. The company was formerly known as United Insurance Holdings Corp. and changed its name to American Coastal Insurance Corporation in July 2023. American Coastal Insurance Corporation was founded in 1999 and is based in Saint Petersburg, Florida.

financial_summary: American Coastal Insurance Corp is a small-cap financial services business with a $475M market cap on $335M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at -10% over the past three years and -1% annually across the full decade, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome. Operating margins are expanding by +2.0pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 21% against a 8% cost of capital — a 13-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $71M in free cash flow — roughly 21 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders. Cash conversion is thin at 0.66×, however, which raises the oldest question in analysis: are these earnings backed by cash?.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 13× is fortress-like.

Net dilution runs at 0.2% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and insiders hold 51% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 1.6× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
